## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Nirodhavāra* (Ya 9.2.2) is the cessation section within the ninth chapter of the *Yamaka*, the sixth book of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. In the organizational scheme of the *Yamaka*, doctrinal categories in the process section (*pavattivāra*) are methodically investigated through three complementary perspectives: origination (*uppādavāra*), cessation (*nirodhavāra*), and joint origination and cessation (*uppādanirodhavāra*) across the divisions of time [Gal 2003; Nyanatiloka 2007; Ronkin 2005]. Scholars note that this repetitive dialectical treatment reflects an early Buddhist process metaphysics, marking an important development in the analysis of momentary phenomena (*khaṇa*) into origination and dissolution phases (*uppādakkhaṇa*, *bhaṅgakkhaṇa*) [Gal 2003; Ronkin 2005]. SuttaCentral records one translation in one language for this text [SuttaCentral].

Text-reuse analysis conducted by DharmaNexus identifies pervasive formulaic repetition within the Pāḷi Canon, with over 13,000 shared segments across 40 texts [DharmaNexus]. The closest internal textual relationships are with the adjacent sections of the same chapter—namely *Uppādanirodhavāra* (Ya 9.2.3, over 3,300 matches) and *Uppādavāra* (Ya 9.2.1, over 3,200 matches)—as well as the corresponding *Nirodhavāra* sections of other *Yamaka* chapters (such as Ya 5.2.2, Ya 3.2.2, Ya 6.2.2, and Ya 2.2.2) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language automated alignments, DharmaNexus detects conceptual and textual parallels with Sanskrit and Tibetan scholastic literature, including Sthiramati's *Triṃśikāvijñaptibhāṣya* and the Tibetan translation of the *Abhidharmakoṣabhāṣyaṭīkātattvārtha* (D4421) [DharmaNexus].
